key_insight: Local symmetry and domain-wall connectivity let bilayer h-BN slide under electric fields without necessarily reversing its net polarization.
engineering_relevance: Separating interlayer motion from polarization switching could enable selective electrical control of mechanical and ferroelectric responses in layered devices.
method: Molecular dynamics with a machine-learning interatomic potential incorporating field-dependent electric enthalpy.
Compare monodomains, isolated domain walls, and reconstructed moiré networks.
Apply changing vector electric fields to probe sliding, wall motion, and domain conversion.
evidence_signal: Simulations show that a rotating in-plane field shifts moiré nodes by approximately 1 Å without detectable change in the AB/BA domain-area ratio, attributed to cancellation across threefold-connected walls.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation evidence; experimental validation and sensitivity to defects, substrates, and finite-size effects remain to be established.
paper_title: Symmetry-Gated Sliding: Decoupling Interlayer Translation from Polarization Reversal in Boron Nitride Ferroelectrics
